narr: A retrograding upper level low combined with highly anomalous moisture values allowed for showers and thunderstorms to develop across southeast California and produce several instances of flash flooding along with isolated damaging wind gusts. Showers and thunderstorms began developing across southeast California late in the morning and into the afternoon on the 25th. Some thunderstorms became strong to severe, with one severe thunderstorm producing some damage in Joshua Tree National Park. Showers and thunderstorms continued through the rest of the day on the 25th with additional development again early in the morning on the 26th. No injuries were reported.
ev: A trained weather spotter reported several inches of flowing water over the roadway near SR 177 and Kaiser Road. No damage or injuries were reported.

According to the California Department of Transportation, there were multiple reports of mud and debris covering SR 177 in multiple locations near Desert Lily Sanctuary as running washes flowed over the road, impeding travel. No damage or injuries were reported.
An official with Joshua Tree National Park reported that Lost Horse Mine Road, Keys View Road, and Geology Tour Road were closed due to flooding. No damage or injuries were reported.

According to local officials, Box Canyon Road near Shavers Well was closed due to sand and rock debris across the road due to flooding. Emergency Management also reported that flooding caused some shoulder damage along the road. Timing was estimated from the first call to California Highway Patrol regarding Box Canyon Road at 0408PDT. No injuries were reported.
